actual_header.message:
Fix poststart retirement observation for multiprocessing workers

Read each retained worker's exitcode once and use that observation for both
returncode and reaped status. Preserve native stop order and strict retirement
gates, with the existing controls covering live and exited workers.

conclusion: Only the existing bounded diagnostic observer changes: each original retained multiprocessing Process is observed via pid then its exitcode property exactly once, preserving iteration and field order.

CPython3.12.13 BaseProcess.exitcode uses the POSIX spawn object's inherited nonblocking waitpid(WNOHANG) poll; a live/unstarted child gives None, an exited direct child gives its cached exit code. This proves no descendant retirement.

Both returncode and reaped use that same observation, so zero and nonzero exit codes are reaped while None refuses. No bool(exitcode) shortcut, join, wait, retry, sleep, signal, deadline or lifecycle action is added.
Existing observation exceptions remain failures through the unchanged stop() handler, including a closed Process's ValueError; no new fallback, suppression or Any is added.

Original native stop ordering, original first errors, every retirement predicate, registry/owner/thread/root checks and root-removal/replacement gating remain byte exact outside the one observer hunk.

controls.existing_four_native_stop_cases: Each now retains a multiprocessing-shaped worker without a poll method, with exitcode0 read exactly once, coherent reaped/returncode output and no second observation after cached stop. Every original before/after native-stop assertion remains.
controls.existing_three_unretired_cases: Each original quarantine/writer/runner fault executes and asserts before added process observations. Separate snapshots of exitcodeNone then-9 prove live refusal, negative exit-code reaping and one read per snapshot while retaining the original fault and cached first result.
